build: experimental with the prompt work landed
settings: the maintainer's own: character voice on (Ali G), thinking medium, Strategy
result: PASS on the mechanism. The over-the-window warning is gone and the reply-shortening line appears in its place.
log_before_today: prompt ~2687 tokens + reply budget 2112 = 4799, over the 4096 window by ~703. Ollama keeps the end and drops the start silently - identity, rules, notes.
log_now: clamping the reply budget 2112 -> 1800 (visible floor 600, thinking budget 512 kept whole) so a ~2296-token prompt fits the 4096-token window. No over-the-window warning on any question.
prompt_size_change: about 2690 tokens before, about 2296 now - the slimming saved roughly 390.

questions.text: How do I beat the Bone Hydra in Hades?
questions.reply: generic - keep moving, keep your distance, dodge the big attack
questions.verdict: NOT evidence either way, and this matters
questions.why: There is no Bone Hydra note in the library. Checked: no note has 'hydra' in its name, and the only note whose text mentions a hydra is a Fallout: New Vegas one about an item of the same name. A generic answer here is the correct behaviour - there was nothing to attach. The roadmap entry for this bug cites this exact question as its proof, and that citation is wrong and needs correcting.

questions.text: How do I beat Megara in Hades?
questions.reply: named her dash patterns, punishing her while she recovers, and using boons for burst damage
questions.verdict: PASS - this is note content, not general knowledge
questions.why: Megara does have a note. The answer is built from it, with the character voice on and thinking at medium, which is the exact shape that used to lose its notes.

findings.what: The ring can land on a spot partly hidden behind the Copy and Retry corner buttons

findings.what: The roadmap's proof for the notes-thrown-away bug is the wrong example
findings.detail: It cites a Hades boss question returning a generic answer with fifteen Hades notes attached. That boss has no note. The bug itself is real and separately measured - 22 of 37 questions on the PC test, 3 of 3 on the device - but this example never demonstrated it.
findings.severity: documentation correction, not a code issue
